title: Brake Check & Pad/Rotor Service
subtitle: Inspect first, decide second — I'll keep you safe and never rush torque.
tone: Safety-first live coach. Celebrate inspection DIY. Honest when replacement exceeds comfort. Max 2 buttons. Trust every ~3 steps.

ux_rules.trust_reminder_default: If you're unsure at any point, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

prerequisites: Level ground; know EPB procedure if equipped
parts_checklist: Rotors if needed (pairs on an axle)
DOT fluid matching the cap (only if bleeding)

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Many pads first come due in the 30–70k window — inspect before metal-on-metal.
Trucks that tow eat pads faster — check rears too.
Electronic parking brake rears often need a scan tool. Don't force the piston.
Wear sensors + bedding matter — indie brake specialist is a strong option.
Soft pedal, pull, ABS light, or fluid loss = stop DIY and get help before driving.

visual_assets.shot_description: Gentle rotate of pad + rotor. Safety-orange accent. No crash imagery.
Slow compress; never pry on piston face.
Lower → star torque → pump pedal reminder.
Animated moderate stops — no panic stops.
Icons: squeal / grind / soft pedal → paths.

steps.title: Brake health check-in
steps.coach_encourage: Checking brakes early is peak ownership — proud of you.
steps.personalize: Looking at brakes on your {{year}} {{make}} {{model}} ({{mileage}} mi).
steps.description: Inspection first. Soft pedal, ABS light, or fluid leak? That's a shop/tow path — no heroics.
steps.safety_warning: Pedal sinks, ABS/brake lights on, or fluid leaking — do not drive.

steps.title: Stop — protect yourself
steps.coach_encourage: Calling this early can save a crash. You did the right thing.
steps.description: Don't drive. Arrange a tow or mobile brake tech. Describe symptoms in chat if you want triage while you wait.
steps.safety_warning: Soft pedal or fluid loss = unsafe to drive.
steps.trust_nudge: If you're unsure, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

action_buttons.label: Describe symptoms
action_buttons.payload: Brake emergency: soft pedal / leak / ABS light. What I see:

steps.title: Lift one corner safely
steps.coach_encourage: Slow and steady — jack stands earn their keep.
steps.description: Crack lugs on the ground, jack at the correct point, stand the car, remove the wheel. Magnetic tray for lugs.
steps.safety_warning: Never work beside a tire with the car on a jack alone.

steps.title: Read the pad & rotor
steps.coach_encourage: You're gathering real data — that's how pros decide.
steps.description: Outer and inner thickness (inners often wear faster). Uneven wear, deep grooves, blue spots? Compare to the chart.
steps.safety_warning: Metal-on-metal grinding — replace ASAP; rotors likely damaged.
steps.trust_nudge: If you're unsure what you're seeing, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

variants.description: Also peek at hose cracks and fluid color in the reservoir (don't open unless bleeding).

steps.title: What did you find?
steps.coach_encourage: A photo beats guessing — I'll help you call it.
steps.description: 2–4mm: plan soon. Under 2mm or metal: replace now. Photo the pads for coach review, or continue to DIY vs shop.

steps.title: DIY or brake specialist?
steps.coach_encourage: Choosing a shop for safety work is strength, not failure.
steps.description: Simple floating fronts: solid DIY (~1.5–3h/axle). EPB, seized slides, or bleeding needed → shop is smart.
steps.safety_warning: Brakes are safety-critical. Unsure of torque/EPB/bleed → book a pro.

variants.description: EPB rears may need a scan tool. No tool? Fronts DIY or shop the EPB axle.
variants.coach_encourage: Skipping a forced EPB retract is the pro move.

steps.title: Replace pads (rotors if needed)
steps.coach_encourage: One caliper at a time — you've got this.
steps.description: Hang the caliper — don't stress the hose. Compress slowly, install hardware/pads/rotor, torque caliper bolts to spec.
steps.safety_warning: Never twist the brake hose. DOT fluid strips paint — keep it off panels.
steps.trust_nudge: If the piston won't move or you're unsure, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

steps.title: Stuck piston or slides
steps.coach_encourage: Backing out now protects the hose and your wallet.
steps.description: Don't hammer the piston. Check EPB service mode. Seized slides often mean a shop caliper. Safer to book help than crack a casting.
steps.safety_warning: Forcing an EPB motor can destroy it.

steps.title: Wheel on — torque matters
steps.coach_encourage: Almost done — pedal feel is the final exam.
steps.description: Snug on the stand, lower, star-torque to door-sticker spec. Pump the pedal until firm before you move.
steps.safety_warning: Soft pedal after pumping — do not drive.
steps.trust_nudge: If the pedal stays soft and you're unsure, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

action_buttons.label: Pedal still soft
action_buttons.payload: After brake work my pedal is soft. Walk me through safe checks before driving.

steps.title: Bed-in & log
steps.coach_encourage: You treated a safety system with respect. Nice work.
steps.personalize: I'll nudge you to re-torque lugs on your {{make}} in 25–50 miles.
steps.description: Gentle bed-in stops from ~35–45 mph — no panic stops. Log pads/rotors + mileage.
steps.safety_warning: Extra following distance on the first drive. Pull over if smell or pedal feel changes.

action_buttons.label: Show bed-in details
action_buttons.payload: Give me a clear bed-in procedure for new brake pads on my vehicle.

completion.title: Brake service wrapped
completion.coach_encourage: Drive gently at first — you earned that confidence.
completion.description: Re-torque lugs after 25–50 miles. Next inspection often with tire rotation (~5–8k).

action_buttons.label: Still have a noise
action_buttons.payload: I still hear a brake noise after service. Help me narrow it down.
